neighbours.label: intensifying/hedging adverb before a verb or predicate: ' literally', ' essentially', ' basically', ' practically'
fire: After the storm, the river literally swallowed half of the village road.
Our tiny kitchen essentially doubles as the office during the week.
By noon the parking lot was literally full of tour buses.
The update essentially removes every reason to buy the premium plan.
For three weeks he basically lived on toast and coffee.
In that heat the asphalt literally melted under the tires.
The merger essentially turned two rivals into a single firm.
The kids practically begged us to stay another night.
quiet: After the storm, crews slowly cleared half of the village road.
Our tiny kitchen also serves as a pantry during the winter.
By noon the parking lot was busy with tour buses.
The update finally removes the old login screen from the app.
For three weeks he quietly worked from his sister's flat.
In that heat the workers repaved the road near the school.
The merger officially closed after two years of talks.
The kids happily waved to us from the back seat.

notes: Card: ' literally' x18, ' essentially' x4 of the top 32; output promotes the same adverbs. Probed ' basically' ~0.33 too.
